review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–76). It has two functor/natural-iso definitions, one naturality theorem (proved by a single `exact` of the adjunction unit's naturality) and one wrapper that supplies instances. It contains no `simp` attributes, no `simp` calls and no rewrite rules. So there is no existing simp rule to be oriented badly, to compete with another rule, or to cycle. I also looked for uses elsewhere. `rightSheafFunctor`, `rightSheafNatIso` and `rightSheafificationUnit_naturality` are used in `RingedSpacePullback.lean` and in the `RingedSpacesTests` files, and I found no `simp` use that needs missing lemmas. The sibling `SheafChangeOfRings.lean` defines `tensorSheafFunctor` and `moduleSheafification` with no `@[simp]` lemmas either, so this file follows the existing convention. Adding `@[simps]` or `@[simp]` here would rest only on the identities looking simple. The rubric advises against that and I found no concrete expression, normal form or practical use that would benefit. The remaining uncertainty is that I did not check every downstream use in the repository. I also cannot run Lean to see whether the proofs that unfold these definitions are awkward.
